title: The Power of the Collection Habit
coreMove: Capture each open loop at the moment it appears so your mind stops rehearsing it as a substitute for control.
sourcePressure: This principles chapter explains why the habit of collecting open loops clears commitments out of the head and reduces psychic drag.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Repeating the mechanics of Chapter 5 instead of showing why capture itself changes mental load.
sourceAnchorNote: The source sidecar contains no chapter-specific named people, named studies, or named places. Use only the listed GTD terms, official metadata, or supported artifacts; do not invent anecdotes.

sourceAnchors.name: psychic drag
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar identifies reduced psychic drag as the principle-level benefit of collection.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Psychic drag is what a commitment costs before you even work on it.

sourceAnchors.name: collection habit
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar frames capture as a habit that gets open loops out of the head.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The habit matters because the capture happens when the loop appears, not later after it has stolen half your attention.

hook: stress is not about having too much to do
a messy desk proves the system is broken
counterintuition: the real problem is not time but attention
this is not about doing more but doing what matters
the simple move is actually the powerful one
tryThisNow: set a timer and write everything down
pick one task and make it specific
review your list and choose a priority
examples: timestamp plus name plus laptop plus decision repeated across all six examples
home kitchen clutter as mental-load shorthand

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: a neonatal unit social worker after a family meeting
exampleSpecs.audience: a social worker holding sensitive follow-ups in a high-interruption setting
exampleSpecs.stakes: a benefits call could vanish during the next urgent conversation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The hand sanitizer is still wet on Rebecca’s palms when she writes the benefits call into her capture notebook before entering the next room.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: wet hand sanitizer shine under corridor lights

exampleSpecs.domain: a freelance stage rigger driving home after load-out
exampleSpecs.audience: a technician whose commitments surface after physical exhaustion
exampleSpecs.stakes: a rebooking lead could disappear because he trusts a tired drive home
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The loading dock gate rattles shut behind Matthew as he records the rebooking lead before the van leaves the curb.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a loading dock gate rattling down

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school choir director during concert rehearsal
exampleSpecs.audience: a teacher whose attention keeps snagging on unwritten reminders
exampleSpecs.stakes: a riser repair could stay mental and become a safety issue
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Pause once," Lea tells the pianist, captures four reminders, and hears the next measure cleanly for the first time all afternoon.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a chipped riser step under stage light

exampleSpecs.domain: a closing attorney mentoring a new associate
exampleSpecs.audience: a lawyer explaining why immediate capture is professional discipline
exampleSpecs.stakes: a document request held for two minutes could cost a closing date
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Niklas one delayed closing to stop trusting the phrase "I will remember" in any client conversation.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a closing binder with a missing-tab gap

exampleSpecs.domain: a restaurant prep lead after a fish substitution breaks service
exampleSpecs.audience: a kitchen lead tracing a failure back to uncaptured verbal changes
exampleSpecs.stakes: wasted product and comped meals can follow from one uncaptured promise
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Where did the substitution really fail: at the grill, or at the moment someone said they would remember it?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a crossed-out fish order on a prep board

exampleSpecs.domain: a reader-facing fifteen-minute capture sweep at a desk, train seat, or break-room table
exampleSpecs.audience: the reader who suspects the method is too simple to matter
exampleSpecs.stakes: they may discover that busyness is partly the cost of holding loops in memory
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You write every claim on your attention without judging it, then notice how few items actually require action in the next five minutes.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a blank index card filling with small obligations

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

skillTargets: explain why capture reduces mental rehearsal
identify fake capture versus trusted capture

tryThisNowSpec: When the next reminder pops into your mind, capture it immediately in the same place you will review later, then return to what you were doing.
